description: eth2-monitor watches a set of Ethereum staking validators for missed/delayed attestations, missed/empty/vanilla proposals, and beacon-API health. Top→bottom = Global → Cluster → Validator. Click 'About this dashboard' (top row, collapsed) for the glossary, effectiveness model, and severity bands.

options.content: eth2-monitor watches a set of **Ethereum validators** — staking nodes that earn rewards for voting on the chain. This dashboard surfaces *how often the validators do their job*, *how on time they are*, and *which ones are struggling*, so a staking operator can spot incidents early and drill down to a single validator without reading raw Prometheus.

Validator
a staked Ethereum node identity (32 ETH bonded) that votes on the chain in exchange for rewards.
Attestation
a validator's vote on what the head of the chain looks like. Each validator attests once per epoch (~6.4 min). Most rewards come from these.
Block proposal
once in a while a validator is picked to produce the next block. Far rarer than attestations, but each one pays a large reward.
Slot
a 12-second time bucket. One slot is one chance for someone to propose a block.
Epoch
32 slots (~6.4 min). The unit Ethereum uses to finalise rewards and penalties.
Cluster
a logical group of validators deployed together (e.g. one customer, one machine, one Kubernetes pod). Comes from the container Prometheus label.
Inclusion distance
how many slots elapsed between when a validator attested and when its vote was included in a block. Optimal = next slot; the larger the distance, the smaller the reward.

- TOP → BOTTOM   **Global → Cluster → Validator**. Fleet KPIs at the top, cluster comparison in the middle, individual validators at the bottom. - LEFT → RIGHT   *Least severe* (delayed votes) on the left, *most severe* (missed votes) on the right. - CLICK TO FILTER   Click a row in the Clusters or Validators table to scope the rest of the dashboard to that container or validator.

Servicewhich monitor instance. Usually one.
Clusterpick one cluster, or All.
Validatordrill to one validator. Usually All except during incident response.
Top Nhow many rows to show in rankings (default 10).
Windowrolling time range for the KPI tiles. Default 24h. Does not affect the 7-day trend (fixed) or per-validator panels (fixed at 1 min).

**Effectiveness** is the one number that tells you whether your validators are doing their job well. It's the product of two simple components: 1. AVAILABILITY   did the validator attest at all? `served / (served + missed)`. 2. TIMING   was the vote included as early as possible? Read from the histogram of inclusion distances. **100%** means every validator attested at the earliest possible slot. Anything below **~98%** indicates a real problem. The **24h KPI tile** (top of the dashboard) reads live; the **7-day trend panel** under "Global health" is the steady SLO signal — single-attestation noise smooths out over a week.
Deeper detail (skip if new): the formal definition is Attestant's ``` effectiveness = (earliest_inclusion_slot − attestation_slot) ÷ (actual_inclusion_slot − attestation_slot) ``` where `earliest_inclusion_slot` skips missed proposer slots so an offline block producer doesn't penalise the validator. eth2-monitor's `canonicalAttestationDistances` histogram is already missed-slot-adjusted to match this definition. See the Attestant link below for the full model.

Colour rules used on every chart and tile:
GREENYELLOWRED
Attester Effectiveness≥99.5%98–99.5%<98%
Proposer Effectiveness≥95%50–95%<50%
Delayed / Miss rate<0.5%0.5–2%>2%
Distance p99<22–4>4
API Errors<1%1–5%>5%

panels.title: When effectiveness drops — what to check

options.content:
Ordered most-likely → least-likely, most-actionable → least-actionable.
TIER 1Your validator software is too slow.
The validator client or beacon node is overloaded, low on RAM, or behind the chain. First check: CPU, memory, peer count.
TIER 2Your validator can't reach peers fast enough.
Network latency from your host to the wider Ethereum network is high. Check peer count and outbound bandwidth.
TIER 3The aggregators are slow.
Aggregators bundle everyone's votes for inclusion in a block. If they're under load, your on-time vote may still arrive late. Not directly fixable from your side; correlates with cluster load and a busy network.
TIER 4The wider network is slow today.
Aggregated votes are reaching block producers late. Least actionable from the operator side.
TIER 5Upstream block proposer missed their slot.
eth2-monitor already corrects for this case, so it won't drop your effectiveness directly — but it correlates with broader network stress.
Work top → bottom when the deficit chart's Distance loss line spikes on a specific cluster.

BeaconScore methodology →
beaconcha.in's "is my validator OK?" score. Operator-facing.
Rated RAVER v3.0 →
Rated.network's effectiveness scoring methodology. More technical than BeaconScore.
Attestant attestation effectiveness →
Canonical write-up that defines effectiveness. Read this for the math and the 7-day-trend rationale.

panels.title: Current Epoch
panels.description: Most recently processed epoch (the just-ended one from the SSE head stream). One epoch ≈ 6.4 minutes, so this tile should tick up about every 6 minutes. If it stops climbing, the monitor or beacon endpoint is stuck.

panels.title: Attester Eff.
panels.description: Attestant effectiveness × availability over the dashboard's selected time range. Effectiveness = earliest_inclusion / actual_inclusion, using the missed-slot-adjusted distance histogram (so a missed proposer slot doesn't penalise the validator). Short ranges are noisy — see the 7d trend panel beside the deficit chart for a stable SLO-grade reading. BeaconScore / RAVER bands: ≥99.5% exceptional, ≥99% target, <98% concerning.

panels.title: Proposer Eff. (24h)
panels.description: RAVER-style proposer effectiveness over the last 24h. (non_empty + 0.25 × empty) / (non_empty + empty + missed). Empty proposals score 25% credit; missed score 0. Reads 'No data' when fewer than 5 proposer duties fell in the window — a 1-of-2 miss on a sparse fleet would otherwise false-red the tile. Window is fixed at 24h (not tied to the dashboard time range) because proposer duties are rare; shorter ranges would read 'No data' more often than not.

panels.title: Delayed Rate
panels.description: Share of canonical attestations whose inclusion distance exceeds the spec-distance-3 tolerance, over the dashboard's selected time range. Tier-2 severity indicator.

panels.title: Distance p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile canonical inclusion distance in shifted slots (0 = spec-distance 1 = optimal). Per container, over the dashboard's selected time range. Tier-3 indicator (Attestant model).

panels.title: API Errors
panels.description: Beacon API non-2xx response share over the dashboard's selected time range, excluding 4xx on /eth/v2/beacon/blocks/{block_id} (those 404s are the canonical missed-proposal signal the monitor relies on, not an infrastructure problem). Infrastructure health, not a validator metric.

panels.title: Attestation deficit (fleet)
panels.description: Fleet-wide attestation deficit over time. 0% = optimal; spikes indicate trouble. Tier 1 (red) = missed, Tier 2 (orange) = delayed beyond tolerance.

panels.title: Attester effectiveness
panels.description: Near-realtime attester effectiveness over a 15-minute rolling window. Effectiveness = earliest_inclusion / actual_inclusion, multiplied by availability. The 15m window is pinned (not $__rate_interval) because the underlying counters only step at epoch boundaries (~6.4 min), so any rate window narrower than ~13 min would oscillate between 100% (no-data plateau) and NaN gaps. 15m always spans at least 2 epoch boundaries and tracks recent fleet behaviour cleanly. Threshold step-lines at the BeaconScore 99.5% and 98% bands.

panels.title: Validator Clusters — top 50 by issue score
panels.description: Per-cluster (container) rollup over the dashboard time range, ranked by issue score = missed + 0.5*delayed_over_tolerance + 0.1*any_delay. Rows depend on the View toggle: Problematic only shows clusters with score > 0; All shows top 50 regardless of score. Click a Container cell to filter the rest of the dashboard to that cluster. Success % = Served / (Served + Missed). Delayed = count of canonical attestations included 2+ slots later than optimal (spec distance ≥ 3, computed from the canonical-distance histogram as count − bucket{le=1.0}); Delayed >tol uses the stricter threshold (spec distance > 3). The three rate columns are each count / (Served + Missed).

panels.title: % missed (per cluster, 1m)
panels.description: Per-cluster attestation miss rate over the last 1 minute. One line per scrape container. Severity bands: <0.5% green, 0.5–2% yellow, >2% red.

panels.title: % delayed-over-tolerance (per cluster, 1m)
panels.description: Per-cluster share of attestations delayed beyond the spec-distance tolerance over the last 1 minute. One line per scrape container. Severity bands: <0.5% green, 0.5–2% yellow, >2% red.

panels.title: Canonical Distance Distribution (missed-slot-adjusted)
panels.description: Snapshot distribution of canonical inclusion distances over the dashboard time range. X = shifted slots (0 = optimal, included at attestedSlot+1). Y = sample count. Histogram panel rendering of the de-cumulated bucket frame; each bar = count of attestations with that shifted distance.

panels.title: Raw Distance Distribution
panels.description: Snapshot distribution of raw inclusion distances over the dashboard time range (before missed-slot adjustment). X = shifted slots (0 = optimal, included at attestedSlot+1). Y = sample count. Histogram panel rendering of the de-cumulated bucket frame; each bar = count of attestations with that shifted distance.

panels.title: Missed Slots In Epoch
panels.description: Missed slots in the most recently processed epoch, per container. ≥3 = network stress signal (chain-wide). If only one container shows this, more likely a monitor stall.

panels.title: Cross-Epoch Attestations (rate)
panels.description: Attestations that were included in a later epoch than the one they attested to. A sustained non-zero rate suggests stale validator-client chain state (Attestant cause #1: generation delays).

panels.title: Empty / Vanilla / Missing-bid Proposals
panels.description: Three MEV-related counters: empty blocks (no EL value), vanilla blocks (proposer didn't use a relay bid), and missing-bid-traces (no tracked relay returned any bid).

panels.title: Request Rate by Endpoint
panels.description: Stacked beacon-API request rate by endpoint ($__rate_interval; auto-sized to viewport). $__rate_interval is used so rate() doesn't underreport during cold-start uptime over a long fixed window (which produces a misleading upward ramp).

panels.title: Error Rate by Endpoint + status_class
panels.description: Beacon-API non-2xx response rate by endpoint and status class (5m).

panels.title: Request Duration p50 by Endpoint
panels.description: Beacon-API request latency p50 by endpoint (10m).

panels.title: Request Duration p99 by Endpoint
panels.description: Beacon-API request latency p99 by endpoint (10m).

panels.title: Duplicate Attestations Skipped (rate)
panels.description: (validator, slot) dedup skip events per second - internal eth2-monitor indicator, not a validator-performance metric.
